subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Elliptical Galaxies
description: A short lesson to help you apply Elliptical Galaxies.

hook.text: Elliptical galaxies are giant balls of old red stars with no spiral arms, no dust lanes, and almost no new star formation.

buildup.text: They range from nearly spherical to football-shaped. The largest ones contain trillions of stars.

discovery.text: IC 1101 is the largest known galaxy—6 million light-years across. It's an elliptical giant in a distant cluster.

twist.text: Most ellipticals formed from galaxy mergers. Two spirals can collide, mix, and settle into a smooth elliptical shape.

climax.text: The Milky Way and Andromeda will merge in 4.5 billion years, likely forming an elliptical galaxy called 'Milkomeda.'

punchline.text: Red, old, and enormous. Born from cosmic collisions between spirals.

quiz.question: How do most elliptical galaxies form?
options: From the merger of two or more spiral galaxies
From gas clouds that never developed spiral arms
From the explosion of supermassive stars in the early universe

details.summary: Elliptical galaxies are smooth, spheroidal collections of mostly old, red stars with little gas, dust, or ongoing star formation. They range from small dwarfs to the most massive galaxies known — giant ellipticals containing trillions of stars.
details.whyItMatters: Elliptical galaxies are the endpoints of galaxy evolution through mergers. The most massive galaxies in the universe are ellipticals, and understanding them reveals the end state of galaxy growth.
takeaways: Smooth spheroidal galaxies of mostly old, red stars
Little gas, dust, or active star formation
Most formed through mergers of smaller galaxies

faq.question: Why are elliptical galaxies red?
faq.answer: They contain predominantly old, cool stars that emit red light. Without significant gas reserves, there's no fuel for forming hot, blue young stars. faq.question: Are elliptical galaxies always formed by mergers?
faq.answer: Major mergers of spirals are the primary formation pathway for large ellipticals. However, dwarf ellipticals may form differently — through harassment by larger neighbors or gas stripping in clusters. Some ellipticals may also form from the collapse of primordial gas clouds in the early universe.
